scope: Complete version-controlled source inventory, deterministic local-fixture verification, four-band risk classification, exact-empty reset validation, fixed-lifetime signed browser sessions, Supabase gateway adapter behavior, database compare-and-swap session semantics verified with deterministic in-memory test doubles, dashboard/API boundary checks, concurrent mutation conflict handling, deployment configuration review, and truthful-claim review.
executionBoundary: All workload scans and cleanup transitions use local demo fixtures. Production browser-session persistence is implemented through the Supabase session gateway and atomic database compare-and-swap; automated tests exercise the server/store contract with deterministic in-memory test doubles and mocked gateway responses, not a live Supabase project. The audit did not verify live Supabase database state, connect to AWS, query CloudWatch or Cost Explorer, deploy a Lambda, execute Kiro Crew/CLI/Web, run a Kiro hook or power, or terminate an AWS resource.
auditedTreeIdentity: The normalized SHA-256 inventory below identifies the complete audited working tree independently of a Git commit. generationBaseCommit records the checked-out generator context before the publication commit and is not a claim that it is the final public commit. The inventory includes every version-controlled/non-ignored project file except this audit artifact itself. The two visible digest-reference lines are normalized to a fixed token before hashing to avoid an unavoidable artifact-hash self-reference; npm run audit:verify checks both the inventory and the displayed artifact digest.

digestReferenceNormalization.rule: Only the one visible Complete audit artifact SHA-256 line in each listed path is normalized before its file hash is calculated.

automatedTestResult.note: Node TAP counts the outer suite in addition to the named nested checks. The standalone gate runs after the TAP suite.

resetAndIdempotencySmoke.boundary: The engine smoke covers local transitions. Browser-facing API tests verify signed fixed-lifetime cookies, and the remote-session path is exercised with deterministic in-memory session-store doubles. Tests cover stale-cookie mutation rejection, stale-read refresh, concurrent compare-and-swap conflicts, one-winner semantics, no-op revision stability, and fixed four-hour expiry. The production adapter signs gateway requests and maps conflict/transport failures safely; gateway transport is unit-tested with mocked fetch responses. These tests do not contact a live Supabase project or independently prove its deployed schema, secrets, Edge Function, or database state. Workload state remains simulated fixture data, not cloud inventory.

deploymentConfigurationReview.apiEntrypoint: api/index.js is included in the complete inventory and passed syntax validation.
deploymentConfigurationReview.vercelConfiguration: vercel.json is included in the complete inventory and passed JSON parsing. It retains framework: null, api/index.js includeFiles, and catch-all rewrite configuration.
deploymentConfigurationReview.resetRoute: Tests exercise POST /api/reset, wrong method, exact JSON content-type enforcement, empty-object-only reset validation, rejected-reset state preservation, reset restoration, a restored subsequent workflow, signed fixed-lifetime session continuity, expiry/legacy fallback, production/Vercel Secure-cookie behavior, and remote-session compare-and-swap semantics using deterministic in-memory store doubles.

sessionPersistenceReview.productionDesign: The Vercel browser-session path requires Supabase gateway configuration and uses a server-side HMAC-signed gateway request. The gateway is expected to validate the signature and invoke restricted session RPCs; the browser cookie contains a session identifier and revision, while fixture transition IDs remain server-side.
sessionPersistenceReview.testedContract: Automated tests use in-memory session-store doubles to verify stale revision rejection, current-state reads, atomic compare-and-swap conflict behavior, idempotent no-op revision stability, and fixed session expiry. The Supabase adapter is tested with mocked fetch responses for success, gateway conflict, transport failure, and server failure.
sessionPersistenceReview.liveServiceVerification: Not performed by this audit. No live Supabase request, deployed Edge Function inspection, database schema/RLS verification, secret-value verification, or production data-plane assertion is claimed.

staticBoundaryScan.note: These static checks support the stated local-fixture boundary; they are not a substitute for an external security review.

claimReview.dashboard: The dashboard fetches same-origin API state and returned workflow/reset data; it renders all four server-defined local risk statuses and does not use timer-only success. Reset Local Fixture Scenario restores only local in-memory fixtures.
claimReview.reset: POST /api/reset accepts only the empty JSON object, rejects non-empty objects before mutation, restores only the browser local-fixture session, and reports that no AWS resource was changed.
claimReview.financialInvariant: The legacy fee expression and independent modern BigInt rational oracle agree across deterministic local property trials. Generated modern fixture code is executed in test against the oracle.
claimReview.kiroAssets: Root .kiro assets exist and label themselves illustrative/unverified. Their presence is not runtime execution evidence.
claimReview.receipt: Receipt digest is a SHA-256 integrity check over canonical local-fixture receipt data; it is unsigned and is not proof of a cloud action.
claimReview.license: Root LICENSE is MIT and the public repository identifies its MIT license.

publicationNote: This audit does not establish Devpost completion, public demo-video publication, entrant eligibility, original-project timing, bonus eligibility, actual Kiro runtime use, or actual cloud actions. It records only the listed local-source evidence.
verification: Run npm run audit:verify and sha256sum docs/audit/necroops-fixture-mode-audit-log.json from the exact source revision.
